name: titration_curve
description: An acid–base titration curve: pH (0–14) against the volume of titrant added, computed EXACTLY from the charge balance (dilution and water included) — never sketched. Choose it for ANY request about titration curves, equivalence points, why the pH jumps, weak vs strong acids or bases, buffers on a titration, pH = pKa at half-equivalence, choosing an indicator, or polyprotic acids. kind: strong_acid / weak_acid (titrated with NaOH) or strong_base / weak_base (with HCl); pka is the ACID form's (acetic acid 4.76; ammonia's NH4+ 9.25), a list for a polyprotic acid. Marks are computed: equivalence point(s), half-equivalence (pH = pKa, weak only), the buffer region (pH within pKa ± 1). compare draws a second curve (a strong acid beside a weak one). v puts a volume cursor on the curve with its readout; animate v ({"animate": {"v": 40}, "duration": 6}) with trace: true and the curve is drawn as the titrant runs in — the marquee move. indicator shades its colour-change range; flask: true adds a burette over a flask whose liquid takes the indicator's colour. Paused, the viewer drags the curve or cursor (the volume), a half-equivalence point up/down (the pKa), an equivalence point sideways (the amount of acid), the indicator band up/down (another indicator), and scrubs or types the numbers written above the plot; an explore beat naming nothing invites exactly this. Numbers for text: {titration.ph}, {titration.v}, {titration.v_eq}, {titration.ph_eq}, {titration.pka}, {titration.ph_half}, {titration.ph_start}, {titration.compare_ph_eq}.
interaction: Scrub the volume added along the curve (or drag the burette down); drag the half-equivalence point (pKa) or the equivalence point (amount); drag the indicator band to pick another.

kind.description: The analyte in the flask (default weak_acid). An acid is titrated with NaOH, a base with HCl.

pka.description: Weak analytes only: the acid form's pKa (acetic 4.76, NH4+ 9.25), or 2–3 rising pKa's for a polyprotic acid ([2.15, 7.20]).

v.description: Volume added at the cursor, mL: draws the cursor with its readout ("12.5 mL, pH 4.76"). Animate it.

trace.description: Draw the curve only up to v (the titration as it happens).

v_max.description: The x axis's end, mL (default about twice the equivalence volume). Set it when animating a concentration.

marks.description: Which computed marks to draw (default all that apply).

compare.description: A second curve in red, e.g. {kind: "strong_acid", label: "HCl"}; unset numbers are the main curve's.

label.description: The main curve's short name ("acetic acid").

analyte.description: The analyte's name in the numbers' line (default "acid"/"base"), e.g. "CH₃COOH".

numbers.description: Write the numbers the curve is made of above the plot (default true) — the viewer scrubs them.

flask.description: Draw a burette over a flask beside the plot.

element_ids.axes: the two axes (their ticks and captions come with them)
element_ids.curve_label: its name, when label is set
element_ids.compare_curve / compare_label: the comparison curve and its name
element_ids.eq_point / eq_label: the equivalence point on the curve and its word (eq_point_2 … for a polyprotic acid)
element_ids.half_point / half_label: half-equivalence, where pH = pKa (weak analytes; half_point_2 …)
element_ids.buffer / buffer_label: the buffer region: the box where pH is within pKa ± 1
element_ids.indicator_band / indicator_label: the indicator's colour-change range and its name
element_ids.cursor / cursor_dot / cursor_label: the volume cursor, its dot on the curve and its readout (when v is set)
element_ids.legend: the numbers' line (its numbers come with it)
element_ids.num_c_analyte / num_v_analyte / num_c_ti: each number in that line (num_pka_2 … for more pKa's) — point at one when the voice names it
element_ids.burette / flask / flask_liquid: the glassware, when flask is true (burette_liquid, burette_tip come with the burette)
element_ids.title: the title, when set

examples.request: Show the titration curve of acetic acid with sodium hydroxide.
Why is the equivalence point of a weak acid above pH 7, unlike a strong acid's?
Titrate ammonia with hydrochloric acid, step by step.
